sections.content: The futuro simple can express predictions and expectations about what will happen. It often appears with words such as *probablemente*, *quizá* or *creo* *que*. The speaker is talking about a future possibility or expectation rather than a fixed immediate plan.

items.english: I will probably travel next year.
I think it will change a lot.
It will be a good experience.

sections.content: *Quizá* can also pair with the subjunctive for a more hesitant prediction (*quizá viaje*) — a form for later. Stated as plainly as it is here, the futuro simple indicative is exactly right.
